Whether a candidate interaction is identifiable at all

Source: R/interactions.R
mm_interaction_rank.Rd

The required invariant, computed before any model is fitted and without needing one to converge. The aliased case is exactly the case that kills rms::lrm() with a singular Hessian, so a check that read the design matrix off a fitted object could never run on the candidate that most needs it.

Usage

mm_interaction_rank(project, frame, pair, nonlinear = NULL, knots = 4L)

Arguments

project

A mm_project().

frame

The development rows, after eligibility.

pair

The two predictor names.

nonlinear

Predictors fitted with splines.

knots

Knots for those splines.

Value

A list with base_columns, base_rank, added_columns, added_rank, identifiable, aliased and reason.

Details

Three outcomes are distinguished, because they are three different facts:

  • the interaction adds columns and the same number of dimensions, so it is identifiable and a test of it means something;

  • it adds columns and fewer dimensions, so some of its terms are aliased with terms already in the model and the degrees of freedom a test would claim are not the degrees of freedom it has;

  • it adds no dimension at all, so there is nothing to test. A p-value here is the most dangerous number in the whole screen: it is near one, it looks like evidence of no interaction, and it is evidence of nothing.

The reduced model's own rank is reported beside them, because a reduced model that is already deficient makes every difference computed against it unreliable, however healthy the increment looks.
